verdict: No significant, material deterioration versus the baseline. The location and cause sections describe the background pattern of the (few) problem arrivals, not a new issue.

evidence: [1] 91% of late trains were already late at 50 St (inherited delay). Origins: at or before 86 St: 21, at 50 St: 2, on approach from 50 St: 2, at or before 59 St-Columbus Circle: 2.
[1] 77% of headway gaps at the target already existed at 50 St.
[2] 100% of late trains were already late at 72 St (inherited delay). Origins: at or before 135 St: 6, at or before 125 St: 2, at or before 72 St: 1, at or before 116 St: 1.
[2] 93% of headway gaps at the target already existed at 72 St.

[3] 100% of late trains were already late at 72 St (inherited delay). Origins: at or before 135 St: 2, at or before 96 St: 2, at 96 St: 2, at or before 116 St: 1. Largest time loss on segment 110 St-Malcolm X Plaza -> 96 St (median +118s vs schedule).
[3] 75% of headway gaps at the target already existed at 72 St.
97% of hours with problems ran fewer than 90% of scheduled trains (overall service delivered 55%): cancellations or missing trips are creating gaps.

[3] Time is lost a little at every stop (135 St -> 125 St +36s, 125 St -> 116 St +21s, 110 St-Malcolm X Plaza -> 96 St +118s, 96 St -> 72 St +60s, 72 St -> target +83s): a dwell-time / crowding pattern rather than one bad segment.
Weekend problem rate is 1.7x the weekday rate; weekend service changes / planned work likely.
20% of problem arrivals occurred during planned service changes (lift 1.7x).
MTA reports 'Planned ROW Work' as 19% of delays on line(s) 1, 2, 3 (0.8x the system share) in the analysed months.
ETAs for problem arrivals drifted 114s on average vs 72s otherwise (1.6x): trains are being held or re-dispatched upstream.
MTA reports 'Police & Medical' as 26% of delays on line(s) 1, 2, 3 (1.2x the system share) in the analysed months.
MTA reports 'Infrastructure & Equipment' as 32% of delays on line(s) 1, 2, 3 (0.9x the system share) in the analysed months.
6% of problem arrivals happened while an MTA 'police' alert was active for the line (problem rate 38% with an alert vs 30% without, lift 1.3x).

recommendations.action: Fill cancelled trips on 1, 2, 3 during the affected hours: check crew availability and car assignments
recommendations.rationale: Fewer trains than scheduled are running in the problem hours.
recommendations.expected_effect: Restores scheduled headways; largest APT lever available.

recommendations.action: Dwell-time programme at Times Sq-42 St and the stops before it during the affected hours: platform controllers, door-closing announcements, step-back crews
recommendations.rationale: Run-time loss is spread across every stop on the approach, the signature of long dwells.
recommendations.expected_effect: Each stop recovers its excess dwell; the effect compounds along the line.

recommendations.action: Check weekend / late-night planned service changes for 1, 2, 3; use alternates other lines at the station
recommendations.rationale: Planned work is announced in advance.

recommendations.action: Check whether scheduled dwell and run times on the approach still match observed loads; re-time the schedule if not
recommendations.rationale: A schedule with unrealistic dwells makes every train late by design.

recommendations.action: Review the general-order (planned work) schedule for 1, 2, 3; add supplement trains or move work windows off the affected hours
recommendations.rationale: Problems coincide with planned service changes.
recommendations.expected_effect: Planned changes stop degrading the analysed hours.

recommendations.action: Set a gap-filling rule: dispatch the next available train from Van Cortlandt Park-242 St when a gap over 12 min forms
recommendations.rationale: A fifth of arrivals follow a large gap.
recommendations.expected_effect: Caps the longest waits, which dominate the APT metric.

recommendations.action: Review dispatcher holding practice upstream of Times Sq-42 St; consider publishing hold reasons in the feed
recommendations.rationale: ETAs drift substantially before problem arrivals, indicating holds.
recommendations.expected_effect: Fewer discretionary holds; more accurate countdown clocks.

sources_used: NY Open Data: trains delayed / incidents
caveats: scheduled counts scaled by observed coverage (536 polling intervals); hours covered < 50% excluded from service delivered
no hour of the day worsened significantly versus the baseline; results describe the whole day
